subject: Final OKR grades + QBR storytelling plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: EoQ prep: grading approach for OKRs + QBR narrative

Team —

With EoQ coming up, I want to lock the approach for final OKR grades and the narrative we'll bring to the QBR. Goal is a lightweight, consistent process so the exec review is about the story and follow-ups, not metric disputes. Proposed plan: 

- Use the scoring rubric we agreed on (0 / .5 / 1 / 1.5) and capture a single "grade" per Objective with 1–2 bullets of evidence.
- Any metric disputes get a short note (owner + data source) and a decision: accept as-is or escalate to product lead.
- I’ll assemble a single CSV of grades; please add one-line narratives for each objective you own.
- Marcus: can you draft 3 narrative bullets we can use on slide 2 (themes + customer impact)?
- Laura: please push the raw numbers into the attached template so I can merge.

Timeline: get grades in by EoD Friday (Mar 27) so I can produce the storyboard by Monday for exec review.

Attachment: [Template stub: OKR_Grades_Q1_2026.csv (CSV)]

If any of you think we need a different rubric this cycle, call it out now — otherwise I’ll assume we’re using the standard.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EoQ prep: grading approach for OKRs + QBR narrative

Thanks Vivek — sounds good. Two quick clarifications: 

1) For aligned/new product bets where the metric is still "leading" (e.g., A/B in flight), do we give a provisional .5 and note next steps toward validation?
2) For the slide storyboard, is Marcus owning the customer-impact framing and I own the executive summary slide?

I attached a short slide outline (starter bullets) and added a placeholder for the exec ask. I can consolidate language after I see the grades.

Attachment: [QBR_storyboard_v1.pptx (PPTX)]

Tessa

Subject: Re: EoQ prep: grading approach for OKRs + QBR narrative

Looping in our numbers — I populated the template with the latest telemetry and my proposed grades. Notes: 

- OKR 1.1 (Hosted API latency): grade = 1.0. Evidence: 95th p90 latency improved by 12% vs baseline; see internal metric ID MET-9812.
- OKR 2.3 (Dedicated adoption): grade = 0.5 (bookings grew but retention not validated). I included a short note recommending a follow-up win-back experiment.
- OKR 3.2 (Private onboarding time): flagged as disputed — I calculated time-to-first-success differently than product. Added a 2-line note and data sources.

I attached the filled CSV and inline notes for the disputed metric so it’s visible in the merged sheet. I’ll be available for a quick sync if we need to reconcile definitions.

Attachment: [OKR_Grades_Q1_2026.csv (CSV)]

Laura Bennett
Director, Strategy & Insights
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: EoQ prep: grading approach for OKRs + QBR narrative

Attached are my notes from the team retro and three short narrative bullets that map to the QBR storyboard. High level themes to surface:

- Efficiency wins: runtime improvements and batching saved ~23% token cost this quarter — position this as unit-economics progress.
- Product-market clarity: Hosted API features drove velocity; Dedicated growth shows demand from regulated customers but we need support scaling docs.
- Risk & mitigation: private deployments took longer than expected; we have a clear ops playbook (see retro notes) and a set of customer commitments to shorten onboarding.

I also pulled a customer quote from Sarah Lee (Acme) praising our latency consistency — I added it under "Customer color" on slide 3. If legal wants a release, we should ping Sarah first.

Attachment: [retro_notes_q1.md (MD)]
Link: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/drive/folders/QBR-2026-Q1

Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Final: OKR grades and QBR storyboard (ready for exec deck)

Thanks everyone — I merged the CSV and updated the storyboard with Marcus’s bullets and Laura’s evidence. Key decisions and next steps: 

- Finalized grades (high-level): 5 objectives at 1.0, 3 at 0.5, 2 at 0 (see attached snapshot).
- Disputed metric (Private onboarding time): we accepted Laura’s definition for the QBR but noted the discrepancy and assigned a post-QBR deep-dive (Owner: Product Ops).
- Narrative: lead with unit-economics improvement (cost/token), follow with Dedicated adoption story, close with the ops remediation plan for Private.
- Exec ask: approval on three resource commitments (one FTE for onboarding, budget for Docs + two external pilot customers).

External: Sarah — thank you for the quote. We’ll label it "Customer color" on the slide and flag with legal for sign-off.

Attachments included: [Final_OKR_snapshot_Q1_2026.csv (CSV); QBR_storyboard_v2.pptx (PPTX)]
Drive link: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/drive/folders/QBR-2026-Q1
HubSpot: HUBSPOT-45678

Action items (owners):
- Tessa: finalize slide 1 executive summary (due Tue EOD)
- Vivek: prepare 90-second talking points for the execs (due Tue morning)
- Laura: coordinate post-QBR metric deep-dive and handoff to Product Ops
- Marcus: confirm permission to use Sarah’s quote (outreach in-flight)

I’ll book a 30m dry-run on Wed morning for anyone who wants to rehearse. Thanks for the quick turn — this is clean and concise.

Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
